CHIEF COMPLAINT
Breast reduction consultation

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Julia Jones is a 25-year-old female presenting for evaluation of bilateral breast reduction. She has been considering this procedure for approximately 6-7 years. The patient reports significant symptoms including chronic back pain, neck pain, and upper back pain that have been present since high school. She experiences bra strap indentations on her shoulders and occasional numbness and tingling in her hands. She reports that her breasts are consistently sweaty but denies rashes underneath. The patient notes that physical activities are limited due to breast size, particularly with exercising, jumping, and running, which cause pain. She currently wears a 34E sports bra as regular bras are uncomfortable and expensive in her size. The patient has been seeing a chiropractor for several years for pain management. She denies prior consultation for breast reduction.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports chronic back and neck pain since high school, bra strap indentations, occasional numbness and tingling in hands, and activity limitations with exercise and running. Denies rashes underneath breasts but reports constant sweating. Denies nipple pain or discharge. Otherwise denies other significant systemic symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No significant past medical history reported. Patient reports being generally healthy overall.

MEDICATIONS
Propranolol for migraine management

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Significant family history of breast cancer. Mother diagnosed at age 40.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is a 25-year-old currently studying psychology. She drinks wine occasionally and denies tobacco and drug use. She has lost approximately 10 pounds over the past few months and desires to lose an additional 20 pounds. She does not have children currently but may plan to have children in the future. She is married; her husband recently accepted a new job and she will be transitioning to his insurance plan in July.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Alert and oriented female, appears stated age
Breasts: Inspection reveals asymmetrical breasts with severe ptosis bilaterally. One breast is slightly lower than the other. No nipple retraction or discharge bilaterally. No breast tenderness, masses, or axillary lymphadenopathy palpable on examination.
Measurements obtained for surgical planning.

RESULTS
Body surface area: 2.65
Schnur scale minimum required resection: 1,792 grams
Insurance: Currently Blue Cross Blue Shield; transitioning to husband's plan in July

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Julia Jones is a 25-year-old female with symptomatic macromastia presenting for evaluation of breast reduction. Patient is an ideal candidate for bilateral reduction mammoplasty. She has attempted nonsurgical treatments with minimal relief. Based on measurements and body surface area, minimum required resection of 1,792 grams is attainable. Given the extremely large breasts, there is potential for using a nipple graft.

Surgical plan: Bilateral reduction mammoplasty with anchor-pattern incision (incision around nipple, straight down, and underneath), tissue removal, and nipple elevation to relieve back pain, neck pain, and improve breast appearance. Anticipated surgery time: 3 hours. Expected postoperative course includes bilateral drains (removed approximately 1 week post-op), overnight hospital stay, clear plastic tape over incisions, activity restrictions for 6 weeks (no heavy lifting), no driving for 2-3 weeks. Target postoperative cup size: small C. Patient counseled regarding potential for altered nipple sensation, breastfeeding limitations (approximately 30% cannot breastfeed post-reduction), and future breast changes with weight gain and pregnancy.

Plan to obtain photographs today. Once patient's insurance coverage changes to husband's plan in July, office will submit for insurance approval. Upon insurance approval, office will coordinate surgery date and patient will return for preoperative consultation to review instructions and address any final questions.
